THC-Hydra through 9.7 contains a stack buffer overflow vulnerability in analyze_server_response() of hydra-http-form.c that allows malicious HTTP servers to corrupt memory via crafted Set-Cookie headers. Attackers can send a Set-Cookie header with an extra leading space followed by a repeated cookie name, causing a negative strncpy length that overflows tmpcookie and crashes Hydra.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user that holds a role with the list_deployment_server capability could access sensitive information from inputs.conf files outside the intended deployment app directory through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API.
The vulnerability is possible because the REST API does not restrict a deployment app name to an existing deployment app before reading input configurations.
For more information see authorize.conf (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/admin-manual/10.4/configuration-file-reference/10.4.4-configuration-file-reference/authorize.conf), Deployment server architecture (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/update-your-deployment/9.0/deployment-server-and-forwarder-management/deployment-server-architecture), and inputs.conf (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/admin-manual/9.4/configuration-file-reference/9.4.16-configuration-file-reference/inputs.conf) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user who holds the "ess_analyst" Splunk Enterprise Security role could store attacker-controlled data in finding exclusion rule metadata. Another authenticated user could later open the Finding Exclusion Rules page. Splunk Enterprise Security could then run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who opened the page. The first user could access data and perform actions available to the later user.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise Security does not escape backslashes in finding exclusion rule metadata before adding the values to a page search.
For more information see Finding exclusions in Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/administer/8.7/user-and-entity-behavior-analytics/finding-exclusions-in-splunk-enterprise-security) and Users and roles for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.7/installation/users-and-roles-for-splunk-enterprise-security) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user who can edit and run a playbook on a permitted label could cause Splunk SOAR to return custom-function status and callback state from another playbook run.
The issue results from insufficient binding between a custom-function-status request and the playbook run that initiates it.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.6.1, 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, an unauthenticated user could determine whether a username exists through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API or Splunk Web and lock out existing user accounts through repeated login attempts.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise returns different login failure responses for locked existing user accounts and nonexistent usernames.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. When a client application enforces step-up authentication or multi-factor authentication (MFA) via a minimum authentication level, Keycloak fails to apply this requirement to login sessions initiated through the credential reset endpoint. An attacker who possesses a user's initial credentials (such as a password) can navigate from the reset interface back to the standard login form and authenticate without completing the required second factor. This flaw allows an attacker to obtain valid access tokens and gain unauthorized access to protected services without satisfying mandatory security controls.

Mongoose Embedded Web Server / Networking Library before 7.24 contains a WebSocket fragmentation validation vulnerability that allows remote attackers to spoof message metadata by sending a single CONTINUATION frame with FIN=1 as the first data frame instead of a required TEXT/BINARY start frame, violating RFC 6455 sequencing rules. Attackers can craft this malformed frame to make mg_ws_cb() in src/ws.c misinterpret the first byte of payload as saved FIN/opcode flags, causing the application to receive a dispatched MG_EV_WS_MSG event with attacker-controlled flags and data truncated by one byte without closing the connection.

Open Robotics RViz PointCloud2Display PointField Out-of-Bounds Read Denial-of-Service Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to create a denial-of-service condition on affected installations of Open Robotics RViz. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the handling of PointCloud2 messages. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of user-supplied data, which can result in a read past the end of an allocated object. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to create a denial-of-service condition on the system. Was ZDI-CAN-32123.

LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. Prior to 0.8.7, POST /api/auth/2fa/verify-temp in api/server/routes/auth.js calls verify2FAWithTempToken and accepts repeated TOTP or backup-code guesses without a dedicated attempt limiter. An attacker must first possess valid primary credentials and a valid five-minute temp token, but can then make repeated second-factor attempts and obtain a full session if a valid code is guessed. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.7.

LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. Prior to 0.8.7, POST /api/auth/requestPasswordReset calls deleteTokens by user ID before creating a reset token, while password-reset and email-verification records in packages/data-schemas/src/methods/token.ts have no populated flow type. When password reset is enabled and email verification is enforced, an unauthenticated attacker who knows a target email can repeatedly delete pending verification tokens and prevent account verification until the unverified account expires. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.7.

WPC Smart Messages for WooCommerce plugin before 4.3.6 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers with Contributor or Author privileges to disclose arbitrary post meta and private product data by supplying attacker-controlled id and key attributes to the [wpcsm_product_field] and [wpcsm_product_data] shortcodes without any capability or protected-meta checks. Attackers can embed these shortcodes in a published post to exfiltrate sensitive order data such as billing email, phone, and address stored as post meta, as well as private or draft product descriptions and purchase notes, exposing confidential customer and business information to unauthenticated site visitors.

LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. Prior to 0.8.6, POST /api/messages/:conversationId authorizes req.params.conversationId in api/server/middleware/validateMessageReq.js but persists attacker-controlled req.body.conversationId through api/server/routes/messages.js. An authenticated attacker can use an owned conversation in the URL while naming a victim conversation in the body, causing an attacker-controlled message to be stored in the victim conversation. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.6.

LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. Prior to 0.8.9, GET /api/permissions/search-principals passes the q parameter to JavaScript RegExp construction and MongoDB regex queries in packages/data-schemas/src/methods/userGroup.ts findGroupsByNamePattern and searchPrincipals without escaping metacharacters. An authenticated user with people-picker permission can submit a catastrophic-backtracking pattern that blocks the Node.js event loop and makes the service unresponsive to concurrent users; invalid patterns can also produce server errors. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.9.

The Shortcodes Ultimate  WordPress plugin before 7.9.1 does not prevent placeholders in a shortcode attribute from being expanded with unescaped nested shortcode output, allowing users with a role as low as contributor to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks.

The Shortcodes Ultimate  WordPress plugin before 7.9.1 does not escape the error message returned when a remote feed cannot be retrieved before outputting it, which could allow users with the contributor role and above to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks against administrators by pointing the feed at a server they control.

The Shortcodes Ultimate  WordPress plugin before 7.9.1 does not restrict which PHP functions a shortcode's filter attribute can call, allowing users with a role as low as Contributor to remove WordPress' term-slug sanitization and perform SQL injection attacks through another shortcode's taxonomy term attribute.

The Shortcodes Ultimate  WordPress plugin before 7.9.1 does not restrict the content type of its lightbox shortcode, allowing users with the contributor role and above to make the lightbox fetch HTML from an attacker-controlled server and insert it into the page unsanitised, leading to Stored Cross-Site Scripting when a user opens the lightbox.

The Shortcodes Ultimate plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Local File Inclusion in versions up to, and including, 7.9.1 This is due to su_get_current_url() interpolating the raw Host request header into the authority portion of a URL that is then passed to esc_url() — which by design preserves '[' and ']' inside the authority so IPv6 literal hosts remain valid — and the [su_qrcode] shortcode substituting that value into its data attribute (the documented %CURRENT_URL% token) before feeding it to do_shortcode(). This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to include arbitrary PHP files that reside within the active theme's root directory (bounded because '/' inside an attribute value terminates parse_url()'s host and is then percent-encoded and stripped), and — when the shipped-default 'Unsafe features' option remains on — to read arbitrary post meta of any post, on any front-end page that renders [su_qrcode data="%CURRENT_URL%"].

Admidio from 5.0.2 before 5.0.17 contains an arbitrary file read vulnerability that allows any logged-in member to read server files by placing local paths in img src attributes of eCard messages. Attackers can send an eCard to their own account so sendEcard() embeds files like adm_my_files/config.php via addEmbeddedImage(), disclosing database credentials and /etc/passwd.

Vikunja from 0.19.0 before 2.8.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows authenticated users to exhaust CPU by supplying unbounded business-day operands in datemath filters. Attackers can send task or time-tracking filters like due_date > now+999999999999b, triggering a per-day loop in go-datemath that pins CPU cores and exhausts the server.

Vikunja from 0.19.0 before 2.8.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows authenticated CalDAV users to exhaust server CPU by uploading VTODO properties with many parameters. Attackers can PUT an iCalendar body with thousands of parameters on one line to any valid project ID, triggering superlinear parsing before permission checks.

Vikunja from 2.6.0 before 2.8.0 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability in the Planka migration converter that multiplies task allocations for duplicate list IDs. Attackers controlling a Planka server can return boards with duplicate list IDs and many cards to exhaust memory and OOM-kill the Vikunja process.

Vikunja 2.3.0 before 2.8.0 contains an uncontrolled memory allocation in the CSV migration module because it does not de-duplicate label column mappings or cap labels per row, and enforces the item limit only after the full import is built. Authenticated users can send one request to /api/v2/migration/csv/migrate with repeated label mappings or many labels per row, exhausting memory until the server is OOM-killed.

SurrealDB 1.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows any user able to run queries to crash the server by triggering unchecked decimal overflow in math::sum or math::product. Attackers can submit a query summing or multiplying large decimal literals or aggregate stored decimals with GROUP ALL, causing a rust_decimal panic that terminates the entire server process.

SurrealDB 3.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains a permission bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated low-privilege database users to read restricted records by calling the GET /export endpoint. Attackers can export raw records that skip table SELECT predicates and field-level SELECT permissions, exposing other users' rows and hidden fields.

SurrealDB from 3.2.0 before 3.3.4 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows record users to update protected rows by exploiting table-level PERMISSIONS FOR update predicates referencing COMPUTED fields. Because check_update_permissions evaluates the predicate before computed fields are populated, the field reads as NONE and deny-intended predicates like blocked != true pass, letting attackers modify records.

ArcadeDB from 26.7.1 before 26.11.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability because LSMTreeFullTextIndex computes BM25 corpus statistics over all buckets of the indexed type, ignoring bucket access control on subtypes. Authenticated users with read access to a supertype but not its subtype can run EXPLAIN or PROFILE on full-text queries and read totalDocs and per-term df values to count hidden subtype documents containing chosen terms.

actix-http 3.18.10 before 3.20.2 contains an HTTP request smuggling vulnerability in its chunked decoder, which treats a bare LF after the last chunk as the start of a trailer section. Attackers can send a body ending in 0\r\n\n through a connection-reusing proxy so the next request's body is parsed as new requests, bypassing WAF or upstream protections.

Heym before 0.0.148 passes Playwright navigate-step URLs to page.goto() without validating the scheme and runs step-based scripts inside the backend container. A signed-in user who can run workflows can navigate to file:// URLs and use getText to read known-path files such as the Kubernetes ServiceAccount token or Docker secrets.

Frappe ERPNext 7.0.0 before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in endpoints that build part of a query from caller-supplied sort parameters without validation. Authenticated low-privilege users can send crafted requests whose sort parameter holds SQL that the database executes as part of the query, extracting sensitive information.

Dockhand before 1.0.57 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability that allows attackers to perform state-changing actions by exploiting missing Origin header validation and absent CSRF tokens. Attackers can lure authenticated users to a same-site attacker page that submits forged POST requests to stop, start, or delete stacks, modify settings, and change credentials.

Dockhand before 1.0.50 contains an improper access control vulnerability that allows authenticated unprivileged users to read restricted data by querying API endpoints lacking RBAC checks. Attackers can access /api/users, /api/license, and /api/hawser/connect to obtain user emails and roles, the full license key, and environment details, while an invalid license grants all users admin rights.

Hysteria 1.0.0 before 2.9.2 contains a denial of service vulnerability in FragUDPMessage where UDP fragmentation fails to handle headers larger than the maximum datagram payload size. Authenticated clients can advertise a small max_datagram_frame_size and trigger a UDP response, causing a slice bounds panic that crashes the server.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the XMT scene loader that allows attackers to access freed heap memory by supplying a crafted XMT file. When xmt_parse_element() replaces an SFNode field child, the freed node stays cached in parser->peeked_nodes and a later DEF lookup passes it to gf_node_get_name(), crashing MP4Box.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in xmt_node_end() in src/scene_manager/loader_xmt.c that writes to freed heap memory when replacing single-node field commands. Attackers can persuade users to process a crafted XMT file where a Conditional node owning the command is unregistered, corrupting heap memory and crashing MP4Box.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the BT/XMT context loader that frees an interaction-type decoder-specific descriptor even when UIConfig re-encoding fails. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene with a BIFSConfig descriptor, causing gf_odf_delete_descriptor() to reuse and free it again, crashing MP4Box and corrupting heap memory.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability because xmt_find_node() in loader_xmt.c resolves DEF names without verifying the node belongs to the current scene graph. Attackers can craft an XMT scene reusing a PROTO node across graphs, causing gf_node_unregister() to read freed memory during teardown, crashing MP4Box and corrupting heap memory.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a heap use-after-free vulnerability in xmt_node_end() that leaves freed child node MFURL fields in the OD link list. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT file with an extra top-level SceneReplace node, causing xmt_resolve_od_links() to read freed memory, crashing MP4Box and corrupting the heap.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in BuddyPress BuddyPress buddypress allows Stored XSS.This issue affects BuddyPress: from n/a through 14.5.4.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in Wetail AB WooCommerce Fortnox Integration woocommerce-fortnox-integration allows Stored XSS.This issue affects WooCommerce Fortnox Integration: from n/a through 4.8.1.

MemberPress Members before 3.3.1, with the Block Permissions add-on enabled, contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows authenticated Author-level users to crash pages by saving a non-string blockPermissionsMessage block attribute. Attackers can store a JSON array in the attribute so wpautop() in get_block_replacement_content() throws a PHP 8 TypeError, causing fatal errors on post, home, search, and REST pages for unauthorized viewers.

anacrolix/torrent before 1.62.0 contains an uncontrolled recursion vulnerability in Decoder.readOneValue in bencode/decode.go that allows attackers to crash the process by supplying deeply nested bencode data. Attackers can deliver crafted .torrent files or magnet link metadata with millions of nested lists to cause a fatal stack overflow, or deeply nested v2 file trees to exhaust CPU.

HedgeDoc before 1.12.1 contains a prototype pollution vulnerability in the POST /history/:noteId endpoint that allows authenticated users to modify Object.prototype by supplying __proto__ as the noteId. Attackers can send a pinned value to /history/__proto__, which historyPost() in lib/history.js assigns onto the prototype, crashing the Node.js process and causing denial of service for all users.

Delta Sharing reference server 1.4.0 before 1.5.0 contains an incorrect permission assignment vulnerability that allows share recipients to read unshared data via container-scoped Azure SAS tokens. Recipients with a valid bearer token can request credentials from the temporary-table-credentials endpoint to read every blob in the storage container, including unshared tables.

Gradio 6.27.0 before 6.32.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in gradio/history.py that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to use the operator's locally saved Hugging Face token by sending a forged Host: localhost header. When ssr_mode is enabled, requests proxied through the local Node SSR server pass the loopback check, letting attackers call run history endpoints to list buckets, read records and assets, and write buckets under the operator's account.
ZTE Z80 Ultra is affected by an unauthorized access vulnerability. Successful exploitation of this vulnerability could result in an impact on integrity.

An authenticated attacker must reach the Edge file APIs through the Leader or directly on an Edge node. On affected managed Edge deployments with RBAC, Read Only access permits these calls. Disclosure is limited to files readable by the Edge process under its operating-system permissions and capabilities.

A flaw was found in QEMU's NBD server. A remote attacker can crash a multi-export NBD server process by exploiting stale metadata export state during an extended BLOCK_STATUS request, resulting in an assertion failure and denial of service.

A flaw was found in QEMU's NBD server. A remote attacker can crash qemu-nbd, qemu-storage-daemon, or qemu-system by sending NBD_OPT_SET_META_CONTEXT or NBD_OPT_LIST_META_CONTEXT with a declared option length exceeding the actual payload, triggering an assertion failure and denial of service.

A flaw was found in QEMU's NBD block driver. A malicious NBD server can send an incomplete structured read reply marked as done, causing QEMU to return uninitialized host heap memory to the guest VM, resulting in host memory disclosure.

Missing authorization vulnerability in the "GetByProject" endpoint (/Project/{id}) of the VulnController in Cervantes version v1.3-beta could allow an authenticated attacker with VulnsRead permission to retrieve the vulnerabilities of any project, even without being a member of it, by supplying an arbitrary project ID.

PagePdfDocumentReader and ParagraphPdfDocumentReader are vulnerable to a denial of service when processing untrusted PDF input.



 The underlying text extraction logic reconstructs layout from a PDF's glyph positions and limits how much memory can be allocated for any single computed gap, but does not limit the cumulative allocation across an entire page.



A specially crafted PDF can exploit this to force excessive memory allocation during processing, resulting in OutOfMemoryError.



Depending on JVM configuration, this can cause request failures with degraded service under repeated exploitation, or immediate JVM termination when ExitOnOutOfMemoryError options are used.



Any application that processes PDFs from untrusted sources (document upload, email attachment processing, RAG ingestion, web crawling) using either affected reader is impacted.

Mattermost versions 11.7.x <= 11.7.13, 11.10.x <= 11.10.3, 11.11.x <= 11.11.3 fail to verify that the requesting user has file download permission under an ABAC policy before reading file content, which allows an authenticated channel member to obtain the contents of files they are denied access to via interactions with an Agent bot.. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00759

A bug related to the Zookeeper HTTP endpoints in Apache Solr allows an authenticated attacker with zk-read permission to read /security.json, bypassing the security-read authorization check. This may cause unauthorized read of credential hashes and authorization configuration.

For this attack to be successful, the following must be true
  *  The system is secured with Solr's Basic Auth plugin
  *  The attacker has gained direct network access to the Solr cluster
  *  The attacker has obtained credentials for a user account with zk-read permission (which is recommended assigned to trusted admins only)


Users are recommended to upgrade to 9.11.0, 10.1.0 or a newer release.
Users who cannot upgrade immediately are recommended to assign the zk-read permission only to users who they entrust reading security.json.

Improper authentication in the emergency login in Devolutions Server 2026.3.14.0 and earlier allows an attacker who holds an administrator emergency code to create multiple persistent administrator sessions via replay of the single-use code on the scripting login endpoint.

Improper access control in the access request approval endpoint in Devolutions Server 2026.3.14.0 and earlier allows an authenticated low-privileged user to self-approve a credential access request via a client-controlled parent request identifier.

Medplum server 5.1.4 before 5.1.42 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in the Binary $presigned-url operation that allows non-admin project members to overwrite other projects' Binary content. Attackers in a project linked to another project can request a signed upload URL with upload=true for a readable Binary and overwrite its stored content, since project ownership is never verified.

msgpack-c C++ library cpp-3.0.0 through cpp-9.0.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the Boost.X3 parser in include/msgpack/v2/x3_parse.hpp when built with MSGPACK_USE_X3_PARSE in reference mode. Attackers can supply crafted msgpack input parsed over buffering iterators so decoded str, bin and ext objects hold dangling pointers, disclosing freed heap memory or crashing the process.

Allocation of resources without limits or throttling vulnerability in Apache IoTDB. Authenticated REST clients can bypass row-limit cap to triggerheap-exhaustion DoS.



This issue affects Apache IoTDB: from 0.13.0 before 2.0.12.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.0.12, which fixes the issue.

Allocation of resources without limits or throttling vulnerability in Apache IoTDB. Authenticated Grafana clients can bypass row-limit cap to trigger heap-exhaustion DoS.



This issue affects Apache IoTDB: from 0.13.0 through 2.0.11.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.0.12, which fixes the issue.

Allocation of resources without limits or throttling vulnerability in Apache IoTDB. Authenticated REST clients can insert large payload to trigger heap-exhaustion DoS.



This issue affects Apache IoTDB: from 0.13.0 through 2.0.11.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.0.12, which fixes the issue.

ToDesktop Builder before 0.36.1 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the todesktop-fs custom protocol handler that allows attackers to escape the bundled files directory using ../ sequences. Attackers who can run script in an application's renderer can issue XMLHttpRequest calls with traversal paths to read arbitrary files accessible to the user.

pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, does not check the token state that GSSContext.unwrap() reports on a GSS-encrypted connection. An attacker on the network path can replay an earlier server packet from the same connection, and the driver accepts it as the answer to the current query. The driver also shares one MessageProp between reading and writing. One integrity-only packet from the server then makes the driver send later SQL and parameters without encryption. Only connections with gssEncMode=prefer or require that start GSS encryption are affected. Versions 42.2.15 through 42.7.14 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, cuts the weight and scale of a BigDecimal to 16 bits when it sends the value in binary, which is the default. The server then stores a different number without an error. For example 999999.99e-262144 is stored as 999999.99, so a tiny value can pass a range check and be stored as a large one. The driver also computes 10 to the power of the scale first, so a short value such as 1e-200000000 keeps a thread busy for minutes. Versions 42.3.0 through 42.7.14 are affected, and 42.7.15 fixes the problem.

Contiki-NG through 5.2 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the MPL multicast engine that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to corrupt memory via unchecked seed ID lengths. Attackers can send near-maximum-size MPL messages with an S=3 option in a short hop-by-hop header, causing data_message_expiration() to write 16 bytes past uip_buf and crash the node.

In AdvertisingData::FromBytes of advertising_data.cc, there is a possible crash due to an unaligned memory access. This could lead to remote (proximal/adjacent) denial of service with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

This could lead to remote (proximal/adjacent) denial of service with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

In ProcessPdu of credit_based_flow_control_rx_engine.cc, there is a possible resource exhaustion due to improper input validation. This could lead to remote (proximal/adjacent) denial of service with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

This could lead to remote (proximal/adjacent) denial of service with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

In ServiceSearchResponse::GetPDU of pdu.cc, there is a possible crash due to an incorrect size calculation. This could lead to remote (proximal/adjacent) denial of service with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

DreameHome cloud API before 2026-10-14 contained an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in the POST /smart-app/meari-cloud/redirectAndLogin endpoint that allows authenticated attackers to obtain another user's Meari camera-platform identity and session credentials by supplying that user's uid. The endpoint used the caller-supplied uid to select the Meari account without verifying that it belonged to the account authenticated by the Dreame-Auth token. Attackers can obtain target uids through public forum profiles and an email-to-uid lookup, and use the leaked credentials to access live video, microphone audio, the camera speaker, and stored recordings of Meari-backed cameras.

DreameHome MQTT broker before 2026-10-26 contained an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers to subscribe to another device's status topic /status/{DID}/{UID}/{model}/# without owning or having access to the device. Attackers who know the device DID, owner UID, and model can receive the device's telemetry, including compressed LiDAR map frames exposing the home's layout, the Wi-Fi SSID and BSSID, local IP address, gateway, firmware version, and the session key used for encrypted video.

An out-of-bounds write issue exists in padded block cipher decryption in AWS-LC. It affects applications that decrypt CBC or ECB ciphertext with PKCS7 padding over multiple calls into the minimum documented output buffer. A remote user who supplies crafted ciphertext might crash the application or corrupt adjacent memory. Affected are all versions of AWS-LC before 5.7.0, AWS-LC-FIPS 4.x before 4.2.0, AWS-LC-FIPS 3.x before 3.6.0, and AWS-LC-FIPS 2.x before 2.0.18.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to AWS-LC 5.7.0, AWS-LC-FIPS 4.2.0, or AWS-LC-FIPS 3.6.0.



AWS-LC-FIPS 2.0.18 is also fixed; AWS-LC-FIPS 2.x reaches end of support in April 2027.

Missing authorization in Kibana Security AI Assistant conversation deletion can allow an authenticated user with access to the assistant to delete other users' conversations in the same space. The delete-all operation can issue a query without an ownership filter using the assistant's internal Elasticsearch client. A user can consequently delete conversation history that they do not own or have permission to modify.

Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value (CWE-789) in Packetbeat can lead to denial of service via a specially crafted, malformed Cassandra protocol message. An unauthenticated attacker who can send traffic on a network segment that Packetbeat monitors can cause Packetbeat to allocate excessive memory and terminate. Elastic Agent is also affected when the Network Packet Capture integration monitors Cassandra traffic, because it uses the same protocol decoder.

Uncontrolled resource allocation in Kibana exception-list filter creation can lead to denial of service. An authenticated user with access to the Security solution can submit a specially crafted request containing a large number of exception-list identifiers. Kibana can create an unbounded number of concurrent operations while resolving those identifiers, exhausting memory and crashing the Kibana process.

Certain Fleet APIs in Kibana expose stored credentials to authenticated users who do not have the Fleet Settings: Read privilege. For example, a user with the Fleet Agent policies: Read privilege can retrieve credentials through Fleet output and agent binary download source APIs. The disclosed credentials could allow the attacker to authenticate to connected backend systems.

Uncontrolled resource consumption in Elasticsearch query parsing can lead to denial of service. An authenticated user with search permissions can submit a specially crafted query containing an excessive number of clauses. Expanding those clauses in memory before enforcing query complexity limits can exhaust heap memory and crash an Elasticsearch node.

Unconstrained S3 endpoint settings in Elasticsearch ES|QL data sources can cause requests containing storage credentials to be sent to an attacker-controlled host. A user with data-source management privileges can configure a custom endpoint without the intended host restriction. On opted-in commercial Elastic Cloud Hosted deployments, the issue can also disclose workload-identity tokens and expose customer cloud resources outside Elasticsearch. Self-managed deployments are affected by the storage-endpoint path only.

A relative path traversal vulnerability in Kibana Fleet and Elastic Agent allows an authenticated user with both Fleet Integrations: All and Agent policies: All privileges to distribute a malicious integration policy to managed Elastic Agents. A vulnerable Elastic Agent processing that policy for a component that runs in an isolated unit can modify or delete files outside the component's intended runtime directory with the privileges of the Elastic Agent process. This can cause loss of files or persistent denial of service on affected hosts.

Missing authorization in the Elastic AI Assistant for Security in Kibana can allow an authenticated assistant user to permanently delete a shared or global Security AI Assistant conversation owned by another user in the same space. The individual-delete path can treat read access to a shared conversation as permission to delete it without checking ownership. The deleted conversation history is lost to its legitimate owner.

An issue was discovered in Elasticsearch where specially crafted compressed payloads can cause an infinite loop. A low-privileged authenticated user can submit a malformed payload to a product API endpoint that causes the node to enter a permanent CPU loop, occupying a request-processing thread indefinitely. This can progressively exhaust the node's processing capacity, degrading or denying access to product features, and requiring a restart of the affected node to recover.

EUSurvey through 1.6, prior to commit 4bf95a3, contains a blind SQL injection vulnerability in the GET /dashboard/surveys endpoint that allows authenticated attackers with the Form Manager role to infer data from the main application database. SurveyService inserts unrecognized sort values directly into the ORDER BY clause of a native query, so attackers can supply SQL expressions and use response timing to infer any data readable by the application's database account, including data outside the surveys listed on their dashboard.

AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. Prior to 0.9.0, nested tools invoked by OrchestratorBlock bypass the main execution queue and are charged only after succeeding, but post-run billing still refunds a failed tool's catalogue price as a presumed pre-flight charge. Any authenticated customer can trigger failed nested calls to add uncharged credits to their balance and fund later executions using the operator's credentials. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.

OpenEMR is a free and open source electronic health records and medical practice management application. Prior to 8.5.0, the staff-facing portal endpoints GET api/onsiteactivityviews and GET api/onsiteactivityview/{id}, mapped to OnsiteActivityView.Query and OnsiteActivityView.Read with p_acl = p_none in portal/patient/_app_config.php, are handled without an authorization check for an authenticated staff session whose bootstrap_pid is empty. portal/patient/_machine_config.php admits that authenticated staff session, and portal/patient/fwk/libs/verysimple/Phreeze/GenericRouter.php applies the route ACL only when bootstrap_pid is nonempty, so the staff request bypasses the p_none check. OnsiteActivityViewController::Query() returns records without patient scoping, and OnsiteActivityViewController::Read() loads a record by identifier without checking ACL or ownership; OnsiteActivityViewReporter::GetCustomQuery() joins portal activity to patient demographics and includes names, dates of birth, addresses, and Social Security numbers. Any authenticated staff account, including one without the patients/demo permission, can therefore read sensitive demographics for patients represented by an existing onsite_portal_activity row; at least one such row must exist for the endpoint to return patient data. This issue is fixed in version 8.5.0.

TastyIgniter is an open-source online ordering, table reservation, and restaurant management system. Prior to 4.4.4, addFromUrl() in src/Flame/Database/Attach/Media.php performs an outbound HTTP request to a caller-supplied URL and stores the response without validating the URL scheme or destination, which could enable server-side request forgery if a reachable feature passes attacker-controlled URLs to the method. The maintainer reports that no shipped first-party feature calls this method and that it is currently unreachable through product functionality, so no current attack path or impact was identified. This issue is fixed in version 4.4.4.
Tanium addressed an information disclosure vulnerability.
Tanium addressed an insertion of sensitive information into log file vulnerability in Connect.
Tanium addressed a denial of service vulnerability in Tanium Server.

rConfig Core 8.1.0 before 8.2.20 and rConfig Pro before 8.4.0 contain a missing authorization vulnerability in ExportController.php that allows authenticated users to export restricted tables. Attackers can supply excluded table names to export($table), bypassing the EXCLUDED_TABLES deny list, and obtain decrypted passwords, device credentials, and API tokens.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in build_frame_code() in libavformat/nutenc.c that allows attackers to corrupt the header_len[] array by supplying inputs with many audio streams. Attackers can remux a crafted input with many audio streams to NUT, causing out-of-bounds reads past static header tables and crashing the application.

FFmpeg through 9.1 contains an insecure default configuration in the zmq and azmq filters of libavfilter/f_zmq.c that binds an unauthenticated command socket to all interfaces on TCP port 5555. Remote attackers can send 'TARGET COMMAND [ARG]' messages passed to avfilter_graph_send_command() to change filter runtime parameters and alter processed audio or video.

FFmpeg 7.1 before 9.1 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in libavfilter/vf_scale.c that allows attackers to read past the filter input array by sending width or height commands using ref variables. Attackers can send such commands via sendcmd scripts or unauthenticated zmq or azmq filters, causing config_props() to dereference an invalid pointer and crash the process.
An off-by-one error in String::WriteOneByte() in Samsung lwnode can cause a one-byte out-of-bounds write when copying a UTF-16 string

Unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability in ITG Bilgisayar Teknolojileri Grubu Ltd. Şti. VSRM allows Using Malicious Files.

This issue affects vSRM: from v14.08.1 before v14.08.5.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in Themefic BEAF beaf-before-and-after-gallery allows Stored XSS.This issue affects BEAF: from n/a through 4.7.22.

Spug before 4.1.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated non-administrator users to read per-host SSH private keys through the GET /api/host/ endpoint. Users granted a host can read the cleartext pkey field returned by Host.to_view and log in directly over SSH, bypassing Spug's permissions and audit trail even after revocation.

GPAC through 26.07.0 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in gf_rtsp_do_deinterleave that allows malicious RTSP servers to hang clients by sending non-RTSP, non-interleaved data. Attackers can answer a client request with a few bytes not starting with '$', 'RTSP', or 'HTTP', causing the RTSP client thread to spin forever and consume a full CPU core.

GPAC through 26.07.0 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in SDP_ParseAttribute that allows attackers to cause unbounded memory growth via a NUL byte in an a=fmtp line. Attackers can supply a crafted .sdp file or malicious RTSP DESCRIBE response to hang gf_sdp_info_parse and exhaust memory, causing denial of service.

GPAC through 26.07.0 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in gf_rtp_parse_mpeg4 that allows remote attackers to crash clients by sending MP4V-ES RTP payloads shorter than 4 bytes. A remote RTP sender or malicious RTSP server can send a short packet after a marker-bit packet, causing an unsigned wraparound in the VOP start-code search loop that reads past the buffer and causes denial of service.

GPAC through 26.07.0 contains an integer underflow vulnerability in gf_rtp_parse_mpeg4 that allows remote attackers to trigger excessive looping by advertising an undersized AU-headers-length. Attackers can send a crafted 22-byte AAC-hbr RTP packet from an RTP sender or malicious RTSP server to run about 2^28 iterations, pinning a CPU core and stalling clients.

Assimp 6.0.0 through 6.0.6 contains an invalid mesh reference vulnerability in glTF2Exporter::ExportMeshes that causes out-of-bounds access when meshes without faces are skipped during export. Attackers can supply a PLY point cloud or degenerate glTF 2.0 TRIANGLE_STRIP model exported to gltf2 or glb2 to crash the application or trigger out-of-bounds memory reads and writes.

Parallels Desktop Handle-based Rename Time-Of-Check Time-Of-Use Information Disclosure Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows local attackers to disclose sensitive information on affected installations of Parallels Desktop. An attacker must first obtain the ability to execute low-privileged code on the target guest system in order to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the implementation of handle-based rename functionality. The issue results from the lack of proper locking when performing operations on an object. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to disclose information in the context of the current user on the host system. Was ZDI-CAN-30608.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in Mamunur Rashid Radius Booking — Booking Calendar for Appointments & Services radius-booking allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects Radius Booking — Booking Calendar for Appointments & Services: from n/a through 1.0.22.
Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in E2Pdf.com e2pdf e2pdf allows Stored XSS.This issue affects e2pdf: from n/a through 2.00.04.

AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. In versions 0.6.5 through 0.10.0, marketplace and shared agents can capture a user's saved SMTP or database login. SendEmailBlock and SQLQueryBlock logged in with the running user's saved SMTP or database credential to whatever server the graph's author put in the node's inputs, with no check that the login belonged to that server. Anyone who publishes a marketplace listing or shares an agent file can capture the saved login of each user who adds it to their library and runs it once, in plaintext. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.0.

BusyBox ftpd Directory Traversal Arbitrary File Read and Write Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to create or delete arbitrary files or disclose sensitive information on affected installations of BusyBox. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the ftpd service, which listens on TCP port 21 by default. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of a user-supplied path prior to using it in file operations. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to create or delete files or disclose information in the context of the service account. Was ZDI-CAN-27555.

browser-use before 1.0.0 contains an allowlist bypass vulnerability in the SecurityWatchdog's _is_url_match function that allows attackers to bypass domain restrictions by exploiting a raw-string startswith() comparison instead of parsed hostname validation. Attackers can craft URLs using userinfo injection or domain prefix confusion (e.g..com@attacker.com or .com.attacker.com) to redirect an LLM-controlled navigation to an arbitrary host, exfiltrating sensitive data such as secrets embedded in the URL to an attacker-controlled endpoint.

LiteLLM key_management_endpoints Missing Authorization Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to bypass security features on affected installations of LiteLLM. Authentication is required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the key_management_endpoints module. The issue results from the lack of authorization prior to allowing access to functionality. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to escalate privileges to resources normally protected from the user. Was ZDI-CAN-32342.

LiteLLM Virtual Key Model Alias Incorrect Authorization Privilege Escalation Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to escalate privileges on affected installations of LiteLLM. Authentication is required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the handling of virtual key model aliases. The issue results from incorrect authorization. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to escalate privileges to resources normally protected from the user. Was ZDI-CAN-32649.

Uncontrolled Resource Consumption vulnerability in Wikimedia Foundation MediaWiki. This vulnerability is associated with program files includes/Search/SearchHighlighter.php. This issue affects MediaWiki: from 1.43.0 before 1.43.12, from 1.45.0 before 1.45.7, from 1.46.0 before 1.46.3, 1.47.

Uncontrolled Resource Consumption vulnerability in Wikimedia Foundation MediaWiki. This vulnerability is associated with program files includes/Media/PNGMetadataExtractor.php. This issue affects MediaWiki: from 1.43.0 before 1.43.12, from 1.45.0 before 1.45.7, from 1.46.0 before 1.46.3, 1.47.

AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. From 0.3.4 before 0.11.0, LLM and other dynamically priced blocks run without charge when a priced input is left at its schema default. An account with a credit balance of zero can make unlimited language-model, code-generation, and image-generation calls at the operator's expense while the platform records the usage at zero cost. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.0.

AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. Prior to 0.10.0, the format Jinja filter in TextFormatter accepts an unbounded width. An authenticated user who can author or run a workflow, or supply its input, can trigger a single synchronous multi-gigabyte allocation that exhausts the executor worker's memory and degrades or denies execution for other users. There is no confidentiality or integrity impact. This issue is fixed in version 0.10.0.

AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. From 0.4.2 before 0.11.0, the E2B code-execution blocks ExecuteCodeBlock, InstantiateCodeSandboxBlock, and ClaudeCodeBlock can leave sandboxes running on the operator's shared E2B credential for up to the sandbox's full timeout, while users are billed only for the block's run time. Any user with a positive credit balance can keep sandboxes running for up to 24 hours on a Pro plan for a flat 1 credit, and each run adds another sandbox. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.0.

AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. Prior to 0.11.0, template rendering is not bounded in size or time. Any signed-up user who can reach a block that takes a format string, such as Fill Text Template or Agent Output, through POST /api/blocks/{id}/execute or the external API's block-execute route, can make the REST API process allocate without bound with one request of a few dozen bytes. This can stop the process from answering any request, including its health check. There is no data read or change impact. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.0.

A flaw was found in the keycloak-services component of Keycloak, which is used for managing authentication and authorization flows. The issue occurs when a client policy is configured to enforce a high-assurance authentication flow requiring OTP. Due to improper validation of existing sessions, a lower-assurance password-only SSO session can be incorrectly accepted if the request does not explicitly demand a specific assurance level. This allows an attacker with access to a user's password or session to bypass the second factor and obtain tokens claiming a higher level of security.

A flaw was found in GStreamer gst-plugins-bad mxfdemux handling of MXF Index Table Segment data. Crafted index metadata can lead to an out-of-range lookup during a seek and terminate the media process. A Fedora 43 test reproduced an assertion-triggered abort. The upstream advisory also notes possible information disclosure, but an attacker-visible leak has not been demonstrated.

A flaw was found in the Keycloak Operator. Deterministic hashes derived from Kubernetes Secrets are published in generated StatefulSet metadata and in KeycloakOIDCClient status. A user with read access to those resources may be able to recover a low-entropy credential referenced by a Secret, even when Kubernetes RBAC denies the user access to the Secret itself.

lightNVR before 0.44.3 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in go2rtc_proxy_authorize_request() that allows authenticated users to access restricted cameras by exploiting inconsistent src parameter parsing. Attackers can percent-encode a second src parameter name or exceed the 255-byte truncation so go2rtc resolves a different camera, obtaining unauthorized snapshots and HLS live streams.

ai-memory 2.6.0 before 3.3.2 contains a symlink following vulnerability in the ai-memory-wikisync companion that allows local attackers to overwrite arbitrary files by planting symlinks at predictable temporary names. Attackers can place a .wikisync-tmp-<page>.md symlink in a shared destination so atomic_write() truncates and overwrites its target with the victim's privileges.

Webmin through 2.670 contains an improper certificate validation vulnerability in generic_ldap_connect in ldap-client-lib.pl that accepts any LDAPS or StartTLS server certificate. Man-in-the-middle attackers can impersonate the LDAP server to capture the bind DN password, often the root DN, and return forged directory data.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a cleartext transmission vulnerability in connect_ldap_db in ldap-server/ldap-server-lib.pl that sends the LDAP root DN password unencrypted when encryption is set to Detect automatically. Passive network attackers observing traffic between Webmin and a remote LDAP server can capture directory root credentials because the connection loop always reaches a plaintext bind attempt.

Webmin through 2.670 contains an improper certificate validation vulnerability in switch_smtp_to_ssl in mailboxes/boxes-lib.pl and status/smtp-monitor.pl, which calls Net::SSLeay::connect without certificate verification or a hostname check. Man-in-the-middle attackers can present any certificate when SMTP with SSL or STARTTLS is configured to capture SMTP AUTH credentials and message content.

Webmin through 2.670 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in ldap-client/check.cgi that allows LDAP directory writers to execute commands via unquoted uid values. Attackers can create a posixAccount entry with shell metacharacters in its uid, executing commands as root when an administrator runs Check Configuration.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a STARTTLS downgrade vulnerability in send_mail in mailboxes/boxes-lib.pl that continues over plaintext when STARTTLS is rejected. Man-in-the-middle attackers can strip or reject STARTTLS to capture configured SMTP AUTH credentials, crackable CRAM-MD5 exchanges, and the content of sent mail.

Webmin through 2.670 contains an improper certificate validation vulnerability in imap_login in mailboxes/folders-lib.pl that skips certificate verification and hostname checks for IMAP SSL connections. Man-in-the-middle attackers can present any certificate to capture IMAP credentials sent by the System and Server Status IMAP monitor and spoof monitor results.

Webmin through 2.670 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in password_change.cgi that allows unauthenticated attackers to change passwords for accounts with empty stored hashes. When passwd_mode is 2, attackers can POST user, old, new1 and new2 with any old value to set a known password and gain access.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a cleartext transmission vulnerability in the SMTP service monitor that never issues STARTTLS because get_smtp_status tests an undefined $ssl variable. Passive network attackers can capture AUTH PLAIN credentials sent in plaintext each time a STARTTLS-configured monitor runs, without needing a Webmin login.

A **NULL pointer dereference** flaw has been found in the acl_check_dns_host_name() and acl_validate_spn_value() functions in source4/dsdb/samdb/ldb_modules/acl.c of the Active Directory domain controller ACL module in the **Samba** package. The checks read the account name after a request that removes it, and they do not test that the value is present. A low-privileged network attacker or user who can update the DNS host name or service principal name of their own computer account can include a removal of sAMAccountName in that same LDAP modify. The directory process crashes. Repeating the modify keeps the directory service unavailable.

A security flaw has been discovered in NASA Core Flight System Limit Checker up to 7.0.1. This affects the function LC_WPOffsetValid of the file fsw/src/lc_watch.c of the component Watchpoint Processing. Performing a manipulation results in integer overflow. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. The pull request to fix this issue awaits acceptance.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway (SCG) Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains an Out-of-bounds Read vulnerability. An attacker with local access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to sensitive information exposure and application instability.

JuggleIM im-server before 1.8.17 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated end users to invoke the internal upd_user_info operation because ImListenerImpl.PublishArrived forwards any client-supplied topic as the RPC method. Attackers holding a valid connect token can supply another user's id to UpdUserInfo to overwrite that user's nickname, portrait, extension fields and settings.

JuggleIM im-server before 1.8.17 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated users to invoke the internal g_del_members operation by supplying it as a client topic. Attackers holding a valid connect token can send crafted WebSocket or HTTP publish requests with arbitrary group and member ids to remove any users from any group in the application.

Remote Mouse for macOS before 3.511 contains a URL scheme validation bypass vulnerability in the opn sub-command of the web command handler, SystemCommandHandler::performWebPanelRemoteFunction_, which checks only for the presence of http:// or https:// substrings rather than validating the actual URL scheme before passing input to NSWorkspace.openURL. Attackers who can reach the TCP command service on port 1978 can send a crafted file:// URL containing a decoy http:// substring to launch arbitrary local applications, open local files with their default handlers, or invoke other applications' registered URL schemes as the logged-in user, requiring no authentication unless a connection password is configured.

openIMIS before 2026-10 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the FHIR R4 module (openimis-be-api_fhir_r4_py) that allows an authenticated attacker with limited district-level access to receive subscription notifications for data outside their authorized scope due to the absence of row-level security checks such as has_perms, get_queryset, ROW_SECURITY, district, or health-facility scoping on the notification delivery path. Attackers can register a standing FHIR subscription to continuously receive claim data and can further direct notification pushes to internal network addresses.

A flaw was found in librelp. When using the GnuTLS driver, an improper error handling vulnerability causes the library to terminate the entire host process upon encountering a Transport Layer Security (TLS) record-level error, rather than disconnecting only the affected session. A remote peer capable of establishing a TLS connection can exploit this flaw by sending a corrupted or invalid record, crashing the host application and leading to a Denial of Service (DoS).

An incorrect authorization weakness in the embedded relation handling of the Laravel MongoDB library may allow a user with basic application privileges to alter records belonging to other users. After an embedded relation is pre-loaded, a routine write on that record is issued without the constraint that limits it to the record the user is permitted to change. This may result in unintended modification or loss of stored data for other users of the same application.

A vulnerability in the MongoDB integration package for the Laravel framework allows an unauthorized user to bypass mass assignment attribute protections. When an application uses attribute deny-lists to guard sensitive model fields, specially crafted request payloads containing database operator keys can circumvent these protections. An unauthorized user with network access to an affected application endpoint can modify guarded attributes, potentially leading to privilege escalation within the application

Ever Gauzy is an open source business management platform for ERP, CRM, HRM, ATS, and project management. Prior to 111.42.9, OrganizationPermissionGuard in packages/core/src/lib/shared/guards/organization-permission.guard.ts checks allowManualTime, allowModifyTime, and allowDeleteTime only when the caller's role is EMPLOYEE and unconditionally authorizes other roles. A tenant administrator who grants ALLOW_MANUAL_TIME, ALLOW_MODIFY_TIME, or ALLOW_DELETE_TIME to MANAGER, DATA_ENTRY, VIEWER, or another non-employee role can therefore leave the organization-wide policy disabled while that role still creates, modifies, or deletes time records, undermining payroll and billing integrity. This issue is fixed in version 111.42.9.

Mongoid builds an incomplete automatic encryption schema for certain embedded document associations. As a result, values that the application declared as encrypted may be written to the database in cleartext, with no error or warning returned to the application. A party holding only basic read privileges on the affected collection, and no access to the encryption keys, may then obtain those values in readable form.

Mongoid does not consistently apply its read-only attribute protection when attribute names are supplied dynamically by the caller. In an application that forwards caller-supplied attribute names into a document update, a user with basic application privileges may change values held inside a field the model declared immutable. This may result in unintended modification of data the application treats as trusted, such as flags used for its own access decisions.

Mongoid contains an incorrect authorization weakness in the handling of caller-supplied filters for bulk removal through a referenced association. Conditions already attached to the association can take precedence over the filter the caller supplied, so records the caller did not select may be removed. A user with basic privileges in an application built on the library may cause unintended removal of records belonging to the same parent record.

Nmap before 7.992 contains an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in the Comm.ReceivePacket function of the NSE rpc.lua library, which buffers ONC-RPC record fragments using the server-declared fragment length without an upper bound. A malicious RPC service on a scanned host can declare fragments of up to roughly 2.1GB, and up to 400 fragments per call, causing the Nmap process to exhaust memory; the read path is reached by rpcinfo.nse during version detection (-sV) and is shared by the NFS, rusers and NetWorker scripts.

Nmap before 7.992 contains an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in the read_db2_packet function of the db2-das-info.nse script, which trusts an unmasked 32-bit length field supplied by the server. A malicious DB2 Administration Server on a scanned host can declare a packet length of up to roughly 4.29GB, causing the script to buffer that much data and the Nmap process to exhaust memory; the script runs during version detection (-sV).

Nmap before 7.992 contains a loop with an unreachable exit condition in the parameter-list parsing of the NSE drda.lua library, which keeps growing its parameter list while processing a malicious DRDA response. A malicious DRDA service on a scanned host can make the loop consume memory without bound on 64-bit builds, exhausting the Nmap process and discarding NSE results for every other host in the same scan batch without reporting an error; the library is reached by service probes during version detection (-sV).

Nmap before 7.992 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in the ConfCreateResponse GCC block parser of the NSE rdp.lua library, which does not check that each block advances the read position. A malicious RDP server on a scanned host can include a single malformed zero-length block in an otherwise valid handshake, causing a permanent 100% CPU hang of the Nmap process that the script-timeout option does not interrupt; the library is used by rdp-enum-encryption.nse in the default script category (-sC, -A).

Nmap before 7.992 contains an excessive memory allocation vulnerability in the unmarshall_array function of the NSE msrpctypes.lua library, which trusts the entry count declared by the server. A malicious SMB server on a scanned host can declare an EntriesRead value of 0xFFFFFFFF with an empty buffer, causing a prolonged CPU spin and exhausting the memory of the Nmap process; the library is used by smb-enum-shares.nse in the default script category (-sC, -A).

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 13.7.0 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user with Maintainer-role permissions to obtain another user's authenticated session cookie and gain unauthorized access to that user's account due to improper session storage handling in the dependency proxy authentication flow when a redirect-pending state was triggered.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab EE affecting all versions from 13.8 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user with Maintainer-role permissions to cause denial of service due to missing server-side input validation on on-call rotation values.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 11.7 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user with Maintainer-role permissions to cause denial of service due to missing resource limits in the error tracking integration.

SeaweedFS is a distributed storage system for files and blobs. Prior to version 4.46, the S3 gateway does not evaluate bucket policies on POST Object uploads, which are multipart/form-data POST requests to the bucket. An authenticated S3 identity that a bucket policy restricts, such as to a key prefix or by source IP, can create or overwrite objects it is denied by sending the upload as a POST instead of a PUT. This issue has been fixed in version 4.46.

Glances is an open-source system cross-platform monitoring tool. In versions prior to 4.5.7, the on-alert action command tokenizer in secure.py treats quote characters as argument boundaries without escaping. A monitored stat value, such as a mount point name, that is quoted in an action command template can contain a quote character that breaks out of its quote boundary and injects additional arguments into the process the action invokes. No shell operator is needed for this attack. This issue has been fixed in version 4.5.7.

Munshi (by Petpooja) before 2026-07-07 contained a broken object level authorization vulnerability in the PUT /api/invoice/{invoice_id}/extracted-data endpoint, which accepts a client-supplied extracted_data object without verifying invoice ownership, enforcing the invoice_edit permission or checking whether the invoice has been soft deleted. Authenticated attackers who know an invoice identifier can overwrite seller and buyer details, invoice identifiers, product entries, totals and custom metadata of invoices, including archived invoices marked is_deleted = 1, undermining the integrity of financial records.

Wallos before 5.11.2 contains an infinite loop vulnerability that allows authenticated users or API key holders to exhaust server resources by storing subscriptions with a frequency of 0. Attackers can trigger renew.php or get_monthly_cost.php to loop forever on a P0D interval, pinning PHP workers and hanging the next-payment cron job for all users.

NodeBB 4.12.0 before 4.16.4 contains an execution after redirect vulnerability in the Intents.create controller that allows unauthenticated attackers to trigger ActivityPub note ingestion. Attackers can send GET requests to /intents/create with a remote note URI in the toPid parameter to inject federated content as local topics and posts.

ProjeQtOr before 13.1.2 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in tool/getAFieldForAClassById.php that allows authenticated low-privilege users to read any object property. Attackers can request Class=User with an administrator id and field=password or email to retrieve password hashes for offline cracking.

The Grow R502-A fingerprint sensor driver (drivers/sensor/grow_r502a/grow_r502a.c) receives sensor responses in the UART interrupt handler uart_cb_handler(). Once the 9-byte header has arrived, the handler reads the 16-bit package length from the header and uses it as the byte count for further uart_fifo_read() calls into rx_buf.data. It never checks that length against the destination buffer. That buffer is a union r502a_packet on the calling thread's stack, set up by transceive_packet(), and is only CONFIG_R502A_DATA_PKT_SIZE + 12 bytes long (140 bytes by default).

A malicious or counterfeit sensor module, or an attacker who tampers with the UART wiring, can reply to any driver command with a header that declares a length of up to 65535 bytes. The ISR then writes that many attacker-supplied bytes past the end of the stack buffer. The existing length check in r502a_validate_rx_packet() runs only after the data has been written, so it does not prevent the overflow. Every sensor transaction is affected, including the ones issued by fps_init() during device initialization.

The result is a stack overwrite with attacker-controlled length and content in the calling thread. This can corrupt control data and may lead to arbitrary code execution on the host MCU, which would undermine any function the fingerprint sensor is meant to protect. The fix validates the declared length against CONFIG_R502A_DATA_PKT_SIZE as soon as the header is complete and aborts the reception if it is out of range.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 12.8 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that could have allowed an unauthenticated user to execute quick actions through Service Desk emails due to improper input sanitization.

A flaw was found in maestro. A remote attacker could exploit a misconfiguration in the gRPC server where authentication defaults to a 'mock' mode. This default setting bypasses all authentication and authorization, allowing an unauthorized attacker to write resource bundles. Consequently, this could lead to arbitrary code execution on managed clusters.

Path traversal vulnerabilities exist in the web-based management interface and API of HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave), which could be exploited by an authenticated attacker with low privileges. Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to read certain files on the underlying operating system.

On Windows, when a connection takes part in a distributed transaction, psqlODBC and its XA library open further connections of their own to finish the transaction. These connections did not keep the security settings of the application's connection:

- When the XA library's first connection attempt failed, it tried again with sslmode=allow, even for a data source configured with sslmode=verify-full or verify-ca.
- The connections the driver opens itself ignored every libpq option given through pqopt, such as channel_binding=require, and the open string it registers with MSDTC carried no pqopt, so the XA library's connections dropped those options too.

An attacker on the network path between the MSDTC host and the PostgreSQL server, without a certificate or credentials, can make those connections go to a server of their choosing without TLS, read and change what they send, and decide the outcome MSDTC records for the transaction.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

psqlODBC mapped an SSLmode value in a connection string that it did not recognise, such as SSLmode=Require, SSLmode=Verify-Full, SSLmode={require} or SSLmode={verify-full}, to disable. SQLDriverConnect() then returned SQL_SUCCESS with no diagnostic, and the connection was not encrypted.

An attacker on the network path of such a connection can read and change its traffic.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

psqlODBC assumed that a table it reads keeps the definition it had when the statement was described or parsed. A database user who owns a table or view another user's application reads can crash that application, with an honest server and default options, in these cases:

- Columns dropped or added in another session while the application updates rows through an updatable cursor, or describes the columns with Parse=1.
- A view whose ctid is NULL, read through an updatable cursor, which writes past the row cache, and a view with a volatile filter scrolled backward with UseDeclareFetch=1.
- Rows added through an updatable cursor to a table with child tables or partitions.
- A column whose type is named lo, written with data-at-execution parameters.
- A DROP TABLE or ALTER TABLE on the connection while another statement still uses the table's column information.
- NULL key columns in rows the driver re-reads for an updatable cursor.
- A function called with more output parameters than its result has columns.
- SQLTables() and SQLTablesW() dereferenced NULL when called with empty strings for the catalog, schema and table names together with a NULL TableType, which kills the process that loaded the driver and every session it serves.

The demonstrated results are crashes; one case writes past a heap buffer, but code execution has not been demonstrated.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

An XML external entity (XXE) vulnerability exists in the web-based management interface of HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave). Successful exploitation could allow an authenticated remote attacker with low privileges to obtain sensitive information from the affected system.

Missing authorization vulnerabilities exist in the API of HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave). Successful exploitation could allow an authenticated attacker with low privileges to modify data on the affected system.

LightRAG provides simple and fast retrieval-augmented generation. Prior to 1.5.5, query responses are cached under a key that omits conversation_history, so an unauthenticated attacker can poison the cached answers returned to other users who send the same query. This issue is fixed in version 1.5.5.

Grav Admin plugin before 1.10.65 contains a password reset poisoning vulnerability in LoginController::taskForgot() that ignores the Require Trusted Host setting when building reset links. Unauthenticated attackers who know an administrator's username can submit the forgot-password form with a forged Host header, capturing the reset token when clicked to take over accounts.

Friendica through 2026.05-1 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in item_edit() that allows authenticated local users to edit other authors' posts by submitting their own stored copy's post_id. Attackers can POST to /item to delete attachments and overwrite the shared body, title and content warning, which is shown under the original author's name.

A SQL injection vulnerability exists in an Accounts Manager service of StellarOne running inside a container due to improper handling of user-supplied input in SQL queries. An attacker with command execution access to the host system or another container with network connectivity to the affected service can send crafted requests to manipulate backend database queries. This issue affects StellarOne: before 5.0.3232.

An OS command injection vulnerability exists in the vShell command-line interface of StellarOne due to improper validation of user-supplied input. An authenticated attacker with access to vShell can inject crafted commands to bypass the restricted shell environment and execute arbitrary operating system commands. This issue affects StellarOne: before 5.0.3232.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, the zone banner-linking page (zone-include.php) does not cast the keys of the includebanner request array to integers. An authenticated manager, or a trafficker with the zone-linking permission, who owns the submitted website and zone can place SQL in an array key, which is concatenated unquoted into the banner-lookup query, resulting in time-based blind SQL injection bounded by the privileges of the application's database account.

A security flaw has been discovered in SourceCodester Online Food Ordering System 1.0. Affected by this issue is some unknown functionality of the file admin/delete.php of the component Deletion Endpoint. The manipulation of the argument id/image_name results in improper authentication. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks.

A flaw was found in bootc. On a sealed composefs boot, a failed bootc-root-setup.service does not fail initrd-root-fs.target, so the initramfs can switch root into the unverified physical root under the original signed UKI.
